name: Tests wait on a condition, not a fixed sleep
instruction: Added test code does not use a fixed sleep to assume that another task, process or tmux pane has progressed.
relevant_when: A patch adds std::thread::sleep, tokio::time::sleep, sleep(Duration...), page.waitForTimeout, or a setTimeout used as a delay, inside a Rust #[test] or #[tokio::test] function, a #[cfg(test)] module, a file under tests/, or a web test file (*.test.ts, *.test.tsx, *.spec.ts).
context: AGENTS.md: do not use fixed sleeps to assume another task has progressed; use a channel, barrier, or an observable predicate with a deadline. CI runs tests in parallel under nextest, so a fixed sleep is a flake source. Allowed: a short sleep as the poll interval inside a loop that re-checks a condition against a deadline, and a sleep whose elapsed time is itself the behavior under test (a timeout, debounce or file mtime granularity) when the code says so.
scope_reason: Existing tests contain sleeps from before the rule; the judge needs the added lines and their surrounding hunk to see whether a sleep sits in a polling loop.

checklist.name: sleep-is-poll-interval-or-under-test
checklist.rule: Each added sleep in test code either sits inside a loop that re-checks an observable condition and stops at a deadline, or is commented as the elapsed time under test. Fail when the added sleep is followed by an assertion or read that assumes progress with no such loop in the hunk.
